summary: Amantadine is an adamantane derivative with two roles: as an antiviral against influenza A (by blocking the viral M2 ion channel) and as an antiparkinsonian agent that enhances dopaminergic transmission and antagonises NMDA receptors, helping rigidity, bradykinesia and levodopa-induced dyskinesias. It is renally eliminated, so the dose must be reduced in renal impairment and the elderly, and it can cause CNS effects (confusion, hallucinations), livedo reticularis and ankle edema. Note: widespread influenza A resistance now limits its antiviral use.
indications: Prophylaxis and treatment of signs and symptoms of influenza A virus infection

dosage.n: Start 100 mg once daily if on other antiparkinson drugs; titrate as tolerated
Occasionally up to 300 mg/day in divided doses

dosage.d: 200 mg once daily or 100 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Begin within 24-48 h of symptoms; continue prophylaxis as advised
Reduced dose due to declining renal function

dosage.d: Reduce dose/frequency per CrCl (e.g. CrCl 15-29: 200 mg first day then 100 mg alternate days)

Take the last dose several hours before bedtime to reduce insomnia

moa: As an antiviral, amantadine blocks the influenza A M2 transmembrane ion channel, preventing uncoating and release of viral nucleic acid into the host cell. In parkinsonism, it increases dopamine release, blocks dopamine reuptake, has anticholinergic-like activity, and antagonises NMDA glutamate receptors - the latter underlying its benefit against levodopa-induced dyskinesia.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to amantadine or other ingredients
monitor: Signs of heart failure and edema

preg: Avoid unless clearly necessary. Amantadine is teratogenic and embryotoxic in animals at high doses, and there are isolated human reports of malformations. Use only if the benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Amantadine is excreted into breast milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the infant, breastfeeding is generally not recommended during therapy.
renal: Amantadine is eliminated largely unchanged by the kidney, so the dose and/or frequency must be reduced in renal impairment to avoid accumulation and toxicity (confusion, seizures). Use creatinine-clearance-based dosing; for CrCl <15 mL/min or hemodialysis, 200 mg every 7 days.
hepatic: Use with caution. Rare, reversible elevations of liver enzymes have been reported; routine adjustment is not specified but monitor in significant hepatic disease.

major: Other anticholinergics (additive confusion, hallucinations, dry mouth)
Live attenuated intranasal influenza vaccine (antiviral activity may blunt vaccine - separate timing)
moderate: Quinine / quinidine / triamterene-hydrochlorothiazide (reduce renal clearance, raise levels)
interactions.diagnostics: May rarely cause reversible elevation of hepatic transaminases and creatine kinase

serious: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome-like syndrome on abrupt withdrawal

monitoring: Mental status, mood and behaviour (including suicidality and impulse control)
Signs of heart failure and peripheral edema
counsel: Do not stop suddenly if taking for Parkinson disease - speak to your doctor first

Approximately 10-25 hours (markedly prolonged in renal impairment and elderly)
Store at 15-30 C in a tightly closed container, protected from moisture
pearls: Influenza A resistance is now widespread - amantadine is generally NOT recommended for current circulating strains; verify local resistance data before antiviral use
Valuable as an NMDA antagonist for reducing levodopa-induced dyskinesias in Parkinson disease
Livedo reticularis and ankle edema are characteristic dose-related effects
Reduce the dose in the elderly and in renal impairment to avoid confusion and seizures
Avoid abrupt discontinuation - withdrawal can cause a parkinsonian crisis or NMS-like reaction
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue as normal - do not take two doses together. Avoid late evening doses to prevent insomnia.
overdose: Overdose (often from accumulation in renal impairment) can cause cardiac arrhythmias, hypertension, severe agitation, hallucinations, seizures and death; anticholinergic toxicity may feature. There is no specific antidote - provide supportive intensive care, ECG monitoring, control seizures, and consider physostigmine for severe CNS anticholinergic effects. Amantadine is poorly removed by hemodialysis.
